builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ERGo: Energy-Efficient Hybrid Graph Neural Network Training on Processing-In-Memory Architectures
summary: The method replaces full-parameter GNN training on processing-in-memory hardware with a schedule that switches mid-training to a low-rank parameter-efficient phase, reducing off-chip memory access and NVM write operations. It requires PIM or heterogeneous NVM-SRAM hardware and introduces a training schedule with low-rank weight approximations, adding implementation complexity. It can fail if the accuracy loss is not negligible on a given task, if low-rank capacity is insufficient late in training, or if the gains do not transfer to the GPU and API infrastructure the reader actually operates.
rationale: The reported gains are measured on PIM and NVM-SRAM architectures that the reader does not have, so the technique is relevant to track but not adoptable on a single 24 GB GPU or through third-party APIs.
technique: Hybrid low-rank GNN training for PIM

It requires PIM or heterogeneous NVM-SRAM hardware and introduces a training schedule with low-rank weight approximations, adding implementation complexity. It can fail if the accuracy loss is not negligible on a given task, if low-rank capacity is insufficient late in training, or if the gains do not transfer to the GPU and API infrastructure the reader actually operates.
Up to 3.15x training speedup, 10.5x energy efficiency gain, and up to 33x NVM lifetime extension on PIM-based platforms.
